items.title: The integrated object-contract-money-maintenance record is the asset a buy-and-build strategy compounds on
items.summary: Vortex Capital Partners became majority shareholder of Bloxs in a buyout announced on 28 October 2024, alongside management and other investors; Bloxs (Utrecht, founded 2015, 35 employees, customers in the Netherlands and Germany including Rockfield, Urban Interest and Burgstate) sells one SaaS system for relationship, building, contract, technical and financial management with API connections to reporting and BI tools. Vortex reports more than €4 billion of annual rent invoiced and more than 500,000 rented properties on the platform, and the thesis is to expand functionality and market position through Dutch and international buy-and-build acquisitions.
items.implication: Judge every acquisition and roadmap item by whether it deepens the shared object, unit, contract, invoice, bank line and ticket model that portals, robots, AI and investor reporting reuse; a bolt-on product that keeps its own data model adds support cost without adding platform value.

items.title: The Informant acquisition brings a VvE and small-manager base that must be migrated without losing trusted service
items.summary: Bloxs acquired Informant Software on 7 July 2025 as its first add-on under Vortex. Informant (Wateringen; custom software from 1990, the Informant product on the market since 1998) serves hundreds of companies: property managers, real estate owners, investors and owners'-association (VvE) administrators, with rental and VvE management in one application. Informant has stopped new sales, its software and support run until 31 December 2027 at the latest, and existing customers get a free, guided migration of data and processes to Bloxs while keeping their contact persons; CEO André Proost describes a phased integration 'without compromising trusted service delivery'.
items.implication: Treat migration tooling, VvE administration parity and support continuity as year-1 product work with their own KPIs (migrated organisations, associations per FTE, retained clients), because the acquired base only becomes platform revenue once it runs on the shared data model.

items.title: Annual rent indexation is a government-set, sector-specific calculation that changes every year
items.summary: For 2026 the Dutch government capped rent increases at 4.1% in the social sector (from 1 July 2026, the three-year average inflation of 3.6% plus 0.5 percentage point, with fixed €25, €50 or €100 amounts for low rents and higher incomes), 6.1% in the regulated mid-rent sector (from 1 January 2026, CAO wage growth of 5.1% plus 1 point) and 4.4% in the free sector (from 1 January 2026, the lower of inflation 3.4% and wage growth plus 1 point); a rent may be raised once a year and never above the contractual or points-based maximum. CBS measured actual rents 4.9% higher in July 2025 than a year earlier (5.1% at housing corporations, 4.7% at other social landlords, 4.4% in the free sector; about 4.1% excluding tenant changes), after the 5.4% of July 2024 that was the largest increase in more than 30 years.
items.implication: Model indexation as a rules engine keyed on sector, contract start date, points ceiling, income class and the yearly government percentages, with letter generation and tenant-portal explanation built in; every mis-indexed contract is both lost income and a Huurcommissie dispute.

items.title: The Affordable Rent Act makes a points calculation part of every new lease and feeds a fast-growing dispute caseload
items.summary: Since 1 July 2024 the Wet betaalbare huur regulates a mid-rent segment of 144 to 186 points under the modernised housing valuation system (WWS), with a points-based maximum rent for everything below 187 points, energy-label deductions and changed WOZ and outdoor-space scoring; since 1 January 2025 landlords must attach a points calculation (puntentelling) to every new lease. Bloxs answered with a certified Huurprijscheck.app integration that sends address, floor area, energy label and WOZ value and stores the WWS score, maximum base rent and PDF report on the unit. The Huurcommissie received more than 18,500 dispute requests in 2024, 30% more than in 2023, including 2,846 points disputes, 4,109 service-cost disputes, 5,746 rent-increase disputes and 5,849 defect disputes, while Huurprijscheck usage doubled to more than 37,000 checks per month.
items.implication: Rent-price compliance is a step in the letting stream, not an annual project: keep points, energy label and WOZ data current per unit, block contracts above the ceiling, and expose the calculation to tenants and owners so disputes are prevented rather than defended.

items.title: Good-landlordship rules turn deposits, contracts, service charges and tenant selection into audited obligations
items.summary: The Wet goed verhuurderschap applies since 1 July 2023: deposits are capped at two months' bare rent and must be refunded within 14 days with deductions limited to arrears, service costs, damage and energy-performance fees; every tenancy needs a written contract; landlords must inform tenants in writing about rights, deposit terms, contact details, service-cost breakdown and the municipal complaints procedure; service charges may only recover actual costs with a mandatory annual statement; discrimination and intimidation are prohibited; since 1 January 2024 a written, transparent selection procedure is required and every municipality runs a reporting point, with administrative fines for violations.
items.implication: Build deposit ledgers with refund deadlines, contract and information-letter generation, itemised annual service-charge statements and a logged candidate-selection trail as standard workflow, so a manager can prove compliance per tenancy to owners and municipalities.

items.title: Every owners' association must fund a reserve from a maintenance plan or 0.5% of rebuild value, which makes MJOP and VvE accounting one process
items.summary: Dutch owners' associations are legally required to reserve for major maintenance in a separate reserve-fund bank account, funded through owner contributions, using either a multi-year maintenance plan (MJOP) that details the work, timing over ten years and costs, or at least 0.5% of the building's rebuild value as stated on the fire and building insurance policy. VGM NL, the trade association for real estate and VvE managers, positions itself as the largest association for companies in real estate and VvE management with almost a hundred members and standard documents and codes of conduct for the trade.
items.implication: Link the installation register and MJOP directly to the association budget, contribution run and reserve-fund ledger, and expose the resulting reserve adequacy to owners in the portal; an administrator who can show compliant reserves per association scales associations per FTE and wins mandates.

items.title: Licensed open-banking feeds plus AI matching move rent reconciliation from month-end to continuous
items.summary: Under PSD2, a regulated provider may access a payment account with the account holder's explicit consent; account information services (service 8) and payment initiation (service 7) are licensed and registered by De Nederlandsche Bank, and all Dutch banks expose the Berlin Group NextGenPSD2 API. Bloxs' certified Yapily Connect integration retrieves bank transactions automatically up to three times a day, and on 6 November 2025 Bloxs launched ClearMatch, an AI reconciliation tool tested for months with large customers that matches incoming payments to contracts, relations and objects, learns from manual corrections and runs continuously in the background rather than only at period end.
items.implication: Measure automated bank reconciliation rate and days to close as the finance north star and treat the bank connector, matching model and dunning as one collection loop; every unmatched payment is a tenant call and a delayed owner statement.

items.title: Structured e-invoicing over Peppol becomes mandatory for B2B by 2030, so supplier invoices and rent invoices must be machine-readable
items.summary: Peppol is the international standard for e-invoicing and e-ordering that the Dutch central government already uses, with e-invoicing mandatory for certain transactions with the Rijksoverheid. On 10 March 2026 the Ministry of Finance sent Parliament an analysis of ViDA implementation that recommends a decentralised Peppol-based model with EN16931 invoices and near-real-time digital reporting, covering domestic as well as cross-border B2B; the proposed timeline is domestic B2B e-invoicing from 1 January 2030, the EU ViDA cross-border obligation from 1 July 2030 and domestic digital reporting around 2032, with draft legislation planned for consultation at the end of 2026.
items.implication: Design accounts payable, rent invoicing and the supplier portal around structured invoices now (Peppol delivery, EN16931 fields, automatic work-order matching), so that the 2030 obligation becomes a switch rather than a rebuild for hundreds of tenant organisations.

items.title: Fault handling runs through partner platforms, so the ERP wins by owning the ticket record and the supplier settlement
items.summary: On 23 July 2025 Bloxs announced a certified integration with Ziezodan in which fault reports registered in Ziezodan flow automatically into Bloxs, status changes are made only in Ziezodan and synchronise back in real time, and Bloxs claims up to 80% fewer administrative tasks. Ziezodan itself reports a 79% first-time-fix rate, 84% tenant satisfaction and more than 42,000 residential units managed daily on its platform. Bloxs' certified partner list also includes Facilitee for service-desk data and Proprli, a Rotterdam collaboration platform for technical property management where owners, managers and tenants handle maintenance, tickets, documents, certificates and suppliers.
items.implication: Keep tickets, work orders, installation registers and supplier invoices as the system of record while letting field platforms own dispatch UX; measure ticket resolution time, first-time-fix and supplier payment time across the integration, not per tool.

items.title: The Dutch private rental stock is shifting from small private landlords to companies and institutions, the natural ERP buyers
items.summary: CBS reports that the private rental sector shrank to 1.18 million dwellings on 1 January 2025, 3,000 fewer than a year earlier and the first decline after three years of growth. Private individuals owned 529,000 rental dwellings (22,000 fewer, mainly through sales to the owner-occupied sector), companies (BV/NV) 419,000 (12,000 more) and foundations and associations 235,000 (7,000 more); institutional owners added about 34,000 units mainly through new construction, transformation and splitting, and conversion to owner-occupation was highest in Utrecht and Noord-Holland.
items.implication: Target investment companies, funds and professional managers whose portfolios grow through construction and transformation, and give them project finance, hand-over into exploitation and owner reporting; small private owners are served through the manager's owner portal rather than as direct tenants of the ERP.

items.title: Germany is a live second market whose Betriebskosten and Mietspiegel rules must be native, not configured around
items.summary: On 10 April 2025 Bloxs announced RDB Real Estate, a German company managing about 1,000 residential units, live on its accounting, CRM, buildings, technical management, contracts, files and reporting modules, with the platform adapted to German processes and regulation and German-language features planned. German tenancy law sets hard deadlines: under § 556 BGB the landlord must issue the annual operating-cost settlement within twelve months after the end of the settlement period or lose the right to a supplementary claim, and the tenant has twelve months after receipt to object. The Mietspiegelreformgesetz in force since 1 July 2022 obliges municipalities above 50,000 inhabitants to publish a rent index (simple by 1 January 2023, qualified by 1 January 2024) and obliges owners and tenants to supply dwelling data on request.
items.implication: Treat country localisation as a product line (German chart of accounts and VAT, Betriebskostenabrechnung with deadline tracking, Mietspiegel-based rent adjustment, bilingual documents) with its own KPIs, because the year-3 German foothold depends on settlement and indexation being as automated as the Dutch flows.

items.title: A 35-person vendor and its 5–200 FTE customers both scale only through hyper automation of the back office
items.summary: Bloxs publishes 5,000+ users, 450,000+ rental units, €4 billion of annual rent invoiced, €70 billion of property value managed and an 8.9/10 support rating; Capterra describes more than 250 real estate organisations managing from 50 up to thousands of residential and logistics units. Customer CRMD Vastgoed Management runs commercial portfolios with staff at the office only one or two days a week and credits automation and AI with removing manual errors and executing tasks at the right moment, reporting that vacancy in newly acquired complexes fell from 30% to below 5% within six to twelve months. On 1 May 2025 André Proost (ex CompuGroup Medical and Centric) became CEO, stating that real estate is digitalising rapidly and Bloxs is well positioned to lead, while founder Dennis Gubbels stays as board member, shareholder and M&A director.
items.implication: Instrument robot and AI-assistant adoption (rent runs, invoice coding, indexation letters, ticket triage) as leading indicators of units per FTE and revenue per FTE for both the vendor and its tenants; professionalising sales, onboarding and support under the new CEO is what turns automation into retained, expanding subscriptions.
